Note::TexAccessor::sqrt_pow¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::sqrt_pow() const

Rewrite Roots As Reciprocal Powers¶

sqrt_pow() rewrites a complete square root \sqrt{x} as (x)^(1/2) and an indexed root \sqrt[n]{x} as (x)^(1/n). Parenthesizing both the radicand and exponent denominator keeps the textual precedence explicit when the rewritten fragment is embedded in a larger expression.

The parser accepts ASCII spacing between the command, optional degree, and required radicand. Square brackets and braces must balance. Nested braces are part of one radicand, and nested \sqrt calls are converted recursively. The degree and radicand are source expressions, not numeric parameters: the method retains their text and does not test whether a degree is zero, simplify powers, or evaluate a root.

Only the complete \sqrt control word is eligible. A longer name such as \sqrted, an incomplete optional group, a missing braced radicand, or text following the linebreak symbol \\ remains unchanged. This preservation rule avoids producing half-rewritten source from malformed editor buffers.

The operation returns a fresh Text Note with identical rank and shape. Cells without complete roots pass through unchanged; empty and undefined states are preserved. Non-Text dtypes reject. Processing is a lexical pass with recursive work proportional to nested root content, and no mutation occurs.

Example 1: Square And Indexed Roots¶

const auto roots = pluss::make_note({R"(\sqrt{x})", R"(\sqrt[3]{a+b})"});
std::cout << roots.tex().sqrt_pow() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["(x)^(1/2)", "(a+b)^(1/3)"]

Example 2: Nested Roots¶

const auto nested = pluss::make_note(R"(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt[3]{a+\sqrt{b}})");
std::cout << nested.tex().sqrt_pow() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"(x)^(1/2) + (a+(b)^(1/2))^(1/3)"

Example 3: Prefixes, Linebreaks, And Incomplete Calls Survive¶

const auto incomplete =
    pluss::make_note(R"(\sqrted{x} + \\sqrt{x} + \sqrt[3]oops)");
std::cout << incomplete.tex().sqrt_pow() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\\sqrted{x} + \\\\sqrt{x} + \\sqrt[3]oops"

Example 4: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\sqrt{a})", "plain",
                             R"(\sqrt[4]{b})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().sqrt_pow() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["(a)^(1/2)", "plain"], 
  ["(b)^(1/4)", ""]
]

Example 5: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().sqrt_pow().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().sqrt_pow();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "roots Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
roots Int64: rejected
